title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos using the faces of Dutch public figures were created and distributed on an online platform. The videos placed victims' faces onto pornographic actors' bodies without consent. Multiple entertainers, television presenters, athletes, government officials, and politicians discovered themselves in these videos and filed criminal complaints.

This represents a failure of platform moderation to prevent the creation and hosting of illegal sexual imagery. The system allowed content to persist and spread despite being classified as revenge pornography and illegal under law. Catching this would have required either technical detection of manipulated media before upload, human review of flagged content, or rapid response to takedown requests from law enforcement or victims.

It is not established how long the videos remained available, whether the platform was aware of them before complaints were filed, or what technical or policy measures the platform had in place to prevent such content.

summary:
Several famous Dutch women are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that attracts 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature digitally altered content of entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Interim Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to news outlets that they have either filed reports or are exploring legal options.

These deepfake pornographic videos work by placing a person's face onto a pornographic actor's body. Experts warn that without government intervention, more fake videos will continue appearing. Deepfake pornography is classified as revenge porn and is therefore illegal. Victims have several options available, including filing criminal complaints so prosecutors can attempt to shut down the websites, starting collective lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued the creator of her deepfake videos, resulting in a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours of community service in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
